messages:
jamie: FYI canary in dedicated pool-A showed p95 jump ~2x after today's merge. Paused rollout. Seeing KV-prefetch scheduler 'ladder' activity spike in traces. @sasha @leo can you take a look?

sasha: saw it on the dashboards — p50 ok, p95/p99 up. Canary only. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/canary/2234 (short link)

leo: I bisected to merge 8572 (scheduler: dynamic-ladder heuristic). Quick profile looks like a ton of time in Prefetcher::Schedule() and a mutex hotpath.

marta: can you paste the flamegraph or a top stack sample?

leo: perf sample (top 3):
```
1) Prefetcher::Schedule() (34%)
2) KVClient::FetchOrEnqueue() (22%)
3) GpuKernelManager::WaitForMemory() (16%)
```
Most of the Prefetcher time is actually repeated enqueues for the same key range.

oncall-bot: Incident detected: dedicated-canary-latency-spike. Auto-pause applied to rollout. Runbook: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/canary-latency

sasha: repro steps I used: ramp clients with seq_len mix {8,64,512} and 30% long tail. On canary the KV miss rate doubles and we see duplicated prefetch ids in the logs.

jamie: hypothesis: dynamic-ladder grouping causes prefetch windows to mis-align across concurrent requests, producing duplicate KV fetches -> extra memory pressure -> kernel scheduling stalls and higher tail latency. Sounds like behavior would only show at specific seq mixes (matches canary).

leo: found duplicates in logs, example:
```
[2026-03-17T21:14:02Z] prefetch: enq id=0x7f3a range=[1024..2047] request=abcd
[2026-03-17T21:14:02Z] prefetch: enq id=0x7f3a range=[1024..2047] request=ef01
```
Same range enqueued twice within 3ms.

marta: can we hotpatch or revert the ladder change? That scheduler landed yesterday. Reverting avoids touching any other perf changes.

jamie: emergency revert seems safest for customer risk. Who can cut the revert PR and run perf CI? Need quick perf baseline before we re-enable rollout.

sasha: I'll cut revert PR now (PR: https://git.redwood/revert/8599). Running perf CI job `perf/staging-latency` (~20m).

leo: local emulation of revert -> run shows p95 drops ~12% on the same workload.

marta: +1 to revert, please include a note in the PR describing flaky prefetch alignment and link to logs. Also add a test plan for ladder behavior.

oncall-bot: CI job perf/staging-latency queued by sasha. ETA ~18m.

sasha: CI finished: perf delta after revert — p95: -11.8%, p99: -9.2%, throughput unchanged. Attaching summary.

jamie: approved, oncall can you deploy revert to canary and monitor 30m?

oncall-bot: Deploying revert to canary now (deploy ID: dply-20260317-0912).

sasha: post-deploy metrics: p95 back to baseline within 5m and stable at 30m. No error spike.

jamie: leaving this as a rollout blocker until we pass extended canary (30m stable) and we have a follow-up ticket to root-cause the scheduler. Creating ticket RED-3245 to track: add tests for duplicate prefetches, add telemetry for prefetch alignment, and explore lock-free enqueue.

marta: also add an integration test with mixed seq_len distributions to CI perf suite, so ladder regressions get caught earlier.

leo: will instrument Prefetcher to emit prefetch-id dedupe metrics and add a small microbenchmark.

sasha: thanks all — great catch. Reopen if we see any regressions. :thumbsup:

jamie: filing customer note and tagging support to follow up with impacted tenant (we paused the rollout so should be fine).

marta: nice quick reaction everyone.
